topic: The Hidden Geometry of Counting: From Ternary Systems to Fractals
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Ternary Foundation
lecture_lines: Ternary systems use three digits: zero, one, two.
They represent choices, not just simple quantities.
Three bits create twenty-seven distinct states.
Think of buttons defining a coordinate system.
This structure builds our foundation for logic.

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Disks move only between adjacent pegs.
State transitions follow ternary arithmetic increments.
Each move adds one to the state.
The sequence maps linearly on a path.
This constrains the Tower of Hanoi.
animations: Display 3 pegs with disks in color #F1FAEE.
Move disk 1 to middle peg using rule.
Move disk 2 to end peg with animation #A8DADC.

sections.title: Mapping the Sierpinski Triangle
lecture_lines: Now, map these moves to two dimensions.
The path traces a Sierpinski triangle.
Each disk expansion grows the fractal.
Anchor points guide the pattern's evolution.
The entire graph reveals the geometry.
animations: Draw a large triangle in color #457B9D.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Deep Connection
lecture_lines: Ternary numbers are our fractal GPS.
They locate vertices within the structure.
The graph represents the total state-space.
Logic and geometry unify perfectly here.
This concludes our hidden geometry exploration.
animations: Overlay Hanoi disk pattern onto Sierpinski vertices.
Fade between Hanoi path and Sierpinski structure.
